[[ ## draft ## ]]
{"to": ["Dana Whitfield"], "cc": ["Victor"], "subject": "Re: Depreciation treatment for new CNC line", "body": "Dana,

Thanks for the details on the CNC line. Quick read before Friday so you have the numbers for the board pack.

For a $1.2M machining line placed in service in Q3, you're looking at 7-year MACRS. My recommendation is to take full Section 179 on the personal-property portion (likely 80-90% of the cost, depending on installation), with 80% bonus depreciation as a fallback for anything that doesn't qualify. That gets you the maximum upfront deduction for federal purposes, which helps Q4 estimated tax payments by reducing taxable income now rather than spreading it out.

One thing to flag: Illinois does not conform to bonus depreciation, but it does allow Section 179. So if we go the Section 179 route, you avoid a state addback — cleaner for your Illinois returns. I'll attach a side-by-side cash-flow comparison showing the Q4 impact under both scenarios so you can see the difference clearly.

I can have the recommendation and the comparison to you by Thursday end of day, ahead of your Friday deadline. Happy to walk through it on a call if that helps with the board discussion.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes", "summary": "Recommends 7-year MACRS with full Section 179 on the CNC line's personal-property portion (80% bonus as fallback) for federal, noting Illinois non-conformity to bonus but allowance for Section 179 to avoid state addback.
